source: Meincke, Mollick, Mollick, Shapiro (2025) Prompting Science Report 2: The Decreasing Value of Chain of Thought in Prompting
finding: On GPQA Diamond, a generic 'think step by step' prompt gives small average gains on non-reasoning models and near zero on reasoning models, at a large time cost. Richer CoT variants (decompose, weigh paths) made no meaningful difference. Gap 1.
numbers: 198 questions x 25 trials = 4,950 runs per model per prompt. Non-reasoning, step-by-step vs direct (average rating): Gemini Flash 2.0 +0.135, Sonnet 3.5 +0.117, GPT-4o-mini +0.044 (ns, p=.067). Versus default no-prompt: Flash 2.0 +0.062, GPT-4o +0.069, Sonnet 3.5 -0.019 ns, 4o-mini +0.004 ns. Reasoning models vs direct: o3-mini +0.029 (p=.024), o4-mini +0.031 (p=.003), Gemini Flash 2.5 -0.033 (p=.005). CoT time cost +35-600% non-reasoning, +20-80% reasoning. On the strict 100%-correct metric 3 of 5 non-reasoning models got worse.
quote: For models designed with explicit reasoning capabilities, CoT prompting often results in only marginal, if any, gains in answer accuracy.
limits: One benchmark (GPQA, science multiple choice, not maths), temperature 0, one simple generic prompt; not Polya-style heuristics; no token-matched comparison (time used as cost). The decompose variant was tested only on GPT-4o at 100 samples.
agent_relevance: Do not add a generic think-step-by-step or decompose heuristic to a reasoning-model core: gain is near zero and it costs time. Heuristic text only pays where the model does not already reason.

source: Gao, Xie, Mao, Wu, Xia, Mi, Wei (2024) Meta Reasoning for Large Language Models (Meta-Reasoning Prompting, MRP)
finding: Letting GPT-4 pick one of seven named reasoning methods per task (CoT, ToT, analogical, self-refine, SPP, step-back, SimToM) gave the best macro average over 7 benchmarks, but no single choice is best everywhere: MRP is second best on 4 of 7 tasks and loses to ToT on GSM8K and Game of 24. Gap 4.
numbers: GPT-4 (gpt-4-1106-preview) macro average: MRP 0.772, ToT 0.725, SPP 0.688, Self-Refine 0.677, Step-back 0.670, CoT 0.654, Analogical 0.648, SimToM 0.640. GSM8K: CoT 0.914, ToT 0.942, MRP 0.921. Game of 24: CoT 0.050, ToT 0.410, MRP 0.310.
limits: Selection accuracy (did it pick the best method?) is NOT reported; only end accuracy. Table columns are garbled in text extraction, so per-benchmark cells beyond GSM8K and Game of 24 should be re-checked in the PDF. Single paper, 2024 models, one run.
agent_relevance: A per-task method chooser can beat any fixed heuristic on average, mainly by avoiding the worst fixed choice. Log which method was chosen and score selection separately.

source: Gao et al. (2024) Meta Reasoning for LLMs: GPT-3.5 results and error analysis
finding: With the weaker GPT-3.5, method selection stops paying: MRP (0.433) is below SPP (0.469) and Step-back (0.452). Authors say the model lacks awareness of its own reasoning ability (scoring errors, self-opinion, factual and reasoning errors). Gaps 4 and 6.
numbers: GPT-3.5 macro average: SPP 0.469, Step-back 0.452, MRP 0.433, Analogical 0.433, CoT 0.416, Self-Refine 0.372, ToT 0.352, SimToM 0.315. GSM8K: CoT 0.831, MRP 0.781 (5 points worse than plain CoT).
quote: the capability of meta-reasoning, like other reasoning abilities, improves as the model becomes more powerful
agent_relevance: A wrong or weak selection has a real cost on a weak core (GSM8K -5 points vs plain CoT). Selection ability scales with the model; a control layer needs a strong judge.

source: Sui, He, Cao, Han, Chen, Hooi (2025/2026) Meta-Reasoner: Dynamic Guidance for Optimized Inference-time Reasoning in LLMs (arXiv 2502.19918 v6)
finding: A separate controller (contextual bandit, LinUCB) reads short progress reports and chooses continue, backtrack, change approach or restart. Ablation removes parts of the controller. It beats asking the LLM itself to pick the strategy. Closest LLM test of 'control layer on top of heuristics'. Gaps 2 and 4.
numbers: Game of 24, GPT-4o-mini: full method 89%; without progress report (full CoT history) 85%; without bandit, LLM picks arm directly 82%; without bandit, plain CoT 4%. Gemini-Exp-1206: 94 / 91 / 87 / 11. Reported baselines: ToT b=5 65%, Reflexion 53%, MACM 80%. MATH-500: GPT-4o-mini 85.6, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B 92.3. Claimed +9-12% over prior SOTA and 28-35% fewer tokens at the same compute budget.
limits: Author-reported; baselines copied from Yao et al. 2023 (older models), not re-run. The 'CoT without bandit' row removes control and strategies together, so it does not isolate control from heuristics. TheoremQA ablation cells garbled.
agent_relevance: Best available LLM evidence that a learned control step adds beyond fixed strategies (+7 points on Game of 24 over LLM self-selection). Control that learns from outcome beats control by asking the model. Still no human-style 2x2 of heuristics only vs control only.

source: Zhuang, Zhang, Si, Zhou, He (2026) Beyond Meta-Reasoning: Metacognitive Consolidation for Self-Improving LLM Reasoning
finding: Splits solving into reasoner, monitor and controller roles and consolidates lessons across instances. Ablation adds components one by one. Gap 2.
numbers: GPT-4o-mini MATH-500: Only Reasoner 72.67, Reasoner+Updates 80.47, Reasoner+Monitor+Control 79.20, full method 85.13 (abstract text quotes 78.93 -> 85.13 against a different baseline); TheoremQA 46.92 -> 55.96. Llama-3.1-8B MATH-500 65.47 -> 76.80. Gemini-2.0-flash 94.93 -> 96.73. Tokens on MATH-500: 1,631 vs 3,200 (CoT-SC) and 3,473 (ToT). Accuracy 84% -> 88% over 5 iterations.
limits: Table layout garbled in extraction; cell-to-row mapping is uncertain, treat ablation numbers as approximate. Small non-reasoning models. Monitor+control (79.20) was not better than prompt-level meta-knowledge updates alone (80.47), so the gain is not clearly from control. Author-run, single paper.
agent_relevance: Monitor and control roles add several points over a bare reasoner on weak and mid models, but a stored-lessons memory adds as much; gain shrinks near ceiling (Gemini 94.9 -> 96.7).

source: Stechly, Valmeekam, Kambhampati (2024) On the self-verification limitations of large language models on reasoning and planning tasks
finding: GPT-4 critiquing its own answers makes results worse; a sound external verifier gives large gains; and re-sampling until the verifier accepts gives most of the gain with no critique text at all. Gap 7.
numbers: 100 instances per domain. Standard prompting / self-critique (LLM+LLM binary feedback) / sound verifier with first-error feedback: Game of 24 5% / 3% / 36%; Graph colouring 16% / 2% / 38%; Blocksworld 40% / 55% / 60%; Mystery Blocksworld 4% / 0% / 10%. Pure re-sampling with verifier, k=25: 42%, 44%, 72%, 14%. Self-consistency over 15: 6%, 14%, 42%, 4%. LLM as verifier: Game of 24 false positive 10.4%, false negative 20.7%; Mystery Blocksworld false negative 97.09%.
quote: our performance increases seem to stem in large part just from having enough guesses and a sound verifier
limits: GPT-4 (early 2024) only; toy domains with exact verifiers. Not maths word problems; no reasoning-model run.
agent_relevance: Polya 'look back' only pays with an outside sound check. Spend tokens on more attempts plus an external verifier, not on critique prose. Self-critique can break correct answers.

source: Kamoi, Zhang, Zhang, Han, Zhang (2024) When can LLMs actually correct their own mistakes? A critical survey of self-correction of LLMs (TACL)
finding: Survey of self-correction papers with a checklist for fair tests. Finds no demonstrated success with prompted LLM feedback outside tasks that suit it, success with reliable external feedback, and success with large-scale fine-tuning. Gap 7.
numbers: No single effect size. Three conclusions: (1) no prior work shows successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs except in tasks exceptionally suited to it, (2) works well where reliable external feedback exists, (3) large-scale fine-tuning enables it.
quote: no prior work demonstrates successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs, except for studies in tasks that are exceptionally suited for self-correction
limits: Survey up to mid-2024, before reasoning models trained with RL on verifiable reward; many reviewed papers used oracle labels or weak initial prompts and so over-state self-correction.
agent_relevance: Matches b25: the verification step needs a tool, test or trained verifier. Treat oracle-label results as upper bounds, not as what the agent will get.

source: Wang, Fang, Mishra and others (2024) Reasoning in Token Economies: Budget-Aware Evaluation of LLM Reasoning Strategies (EMNLP)
finding: When chain-of-thought self-consistency gets the same compute budget, it matches or beats Plan-and-Solve, Least-to-Most, Progressive-Hint, multi-agent debate and Reflexion on most datasets. Gap 1 (equal budget, older models).
numbers: GPT-3.5-0301 on GSM8K, MATH, TheoremQA, HotpotQA, CSQA: CoT-SC beats multi-agent debate and Reflexion at equal tokens; Plan-and-Solve SC and Least-to-Most SC curves are no better than plain CoT SC (read from plots, no table cells). Game of 24: ToT beats CoT-SC only with GPT-4 and a large budget; with GPT-3.5, CoT-SC beats ToT. Debate and Reflexion get worse with more budget; SC does not.
limits: Results are mostly plots; no table to quote. GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 (2024). Not reasoning models. Self-evaluation helps only where the model is calibrated.
agent_relevance: Strong reason to run an equal-token control in any test of heuristics: a repeated plain attempt is the default rival. Heuristic gains in the a, b and c files mostly lack this control.

source: Naik, Chandrasekaran, Yuksekgonul, Palangi, Nushi (2024) Diversity of Thought Improves Reasoning Abilities of LLMs (DIV-SE, IDIV-SE)
finding: The model first proposes several solution approaches (a heuristic list per problem). Sampling one answer under each different approach beats sampling the same prompt several times with majority vote, at similar or lower cost. Gap 8.
numbers: GPT-4, zero-shot CoT: Graph colouring CoT 15.0, SC-10 23.0, IDIV-SE 74.0, DIV-SE 97.0. Blocksworld 3: CoT 70, SC-10 73, IDIV-SE 82, DIV-SE 94. Blocksworld 4/5: 40 / 41.2 / 57 / 69.6. MATH (counting and probability), GPT-4: DIV-SE +14.3 (few-shot, base 66.46) and +16.87 (zero-shot, base 62.24) points; GPT-3.5 +21.84 and +13.04. AQuA GPT-3.5 +14.23 and +16.52. GPT-3.5 on Blocksworld: no gain. Ensemble size 5 (3 for planning).
limits: 2023-24 models; GPT-3.5 shows no gain on hard planning. SC used temperature 0.7 while DIV-SE used T=0; the approach list is made by the model. No reasoning models. Table 2 layout garbled; Table 1 and text used.
agent_relevance: Inference-time heuristic diversity beats same-prompt resampling on this evidence. Strongest support for sampling across different heuristics rather than repeating one. Needs a replication on reasoning models at equal tokens.

source: Hegazy (2024) Diversity of Thought Elicits Stronger Reasoning Capabilities in Multi-Agent Debate Frameworks
finding: Debate among different models (not different heuristics) beats debate among copies of one model. Shows diversity of source matters, but of model, not of method. Gap 8, side evidence.
numbers: GSM8K: Gemini-Pro, Mixtral, PaLM-2 alone 78%, 64%, 70%; diverse debate after 4 rounds 91%; three Gemini-Pro instances 82%. ASDiv: diverse debate 94%. Small-model set: +17% by round 4 versus +10% for the same-model set.
limits: Single small paper in a minor journal; figure text garbled; rounded accuracy figures; tests model diversity, not heuristic diversity. Compare d08, where debate did not beat self-consistency at equal calls.
agent_relevance: Weak support only. If diversity is wanted, vary method and model, but test at equal calls.

source: Li, Liu, Sheth, Viegas, Wattenberg, Pfister (2024) Measuring and Controlling Instruction (In)Stability in Language Model Dialogs (COLM)
finding: A system-prompt instruction decays within about eight dialogue rounds in LLaMA2-chat-70B and GPT-3.5; attention to the instruction falls over long exchanges. Nearest LLM analogue to heuristic decay after training. Gap 9.
numbers: Benchmark of 100 system prompts in 5 categories; 200 two-chatbot conversations with random prompt pairs; significant drift within 8 rounds (curve in figure 3, not tabulated). Split-softmax (attention re-weighting) gave a better stability-performance trade-off than a prompting baseline and a literature method.
quote: we reveal a significant instruction drift within eight rounds of conversations
limits: 2023 chat models; persona and format instructions, not reasoning heuristics. No human-style delayed test. The attention-decay mechanism is a hypothesis.
agent_relevance: A heuristic list placed once in the system prompt cannot be assumed to still steer at step 50. Re-inject or re-check the active heuristic at each state transition. Test with a drift probe.

source: Lin, Zeng, Zhu, Wang, Shun, Wu, Zhou (2026) Plan and Budget: Effective and Efficient Test-Time Scaling on LLM Reasoning (ICLR)
finding: On true reasoning models (R1-distills, QwQ-32B, o4-mini) a small non-reasoning model plans sub-questions and sets token budgets. On MATH-500 accuracy stays about the same and tokens fall; the large gains are on the planning benchmark. Gap 1 (reasoning models, token-aware).
numbers: E3 efficiency metric on MATH-500: DS-LLaMA-70B 4.55 -> 5.89 (+29.4%), o4-mini 13.25 -> 15.95 (+20.3%). TravelPlanner E3: DS-Qwen-32B 0.16 -> 0.47 (+193.8%), DS-LLaMA-70B 0.49 -> 0.93, o4-mini 0.056 -> 0.104 (+85.7%). Abstract: up to 70% accuracy gain, 39% token reduction. Planner is LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct. A global token cap alone cut pass rate at all difficulty levels.
limits: 'Up to 70%' is a relative gain on the hardest benchmark. Per-cell accuracy tables garbled; MATH-500 accuracy described as comparable, not higher. E3 is the authors' own metric. Decomposition plus a budget, not a Polya prompt alone.
agent_relevance: Planning plus a budget helps reasoning models mostly by saving tokens, and by raising constraint-heavy planning scores; it is not an accuracy lift on maths. Supports a cheap external planner with budget control.

source: Schoenfeld (1979) Explicit heuristic training as a variable in problem-solving performance, JRME 10(3) 173-187
finding: Full paper opened. 7 upper-division students; 4 random to heuristics training (five heuristics: diagram, induction, contradiction, fewer variables, subgoals), 3 controls with the same practice problems and same solutions. All 4 trained students outscored all 3 controls. Gap 5 (1979 part).
numbers: Average net gain 0 for controls, over 2 problems for the heuristics group. All 4 trained improved, 1 of 3 controls improved. Chance of all 4 outscoring all 3 is 1/35, so p<.05. Posttest Problem 1: 3 of 4 trained solved vs 1 of 3 control (that one intuited the strategy). Induction posttest: all 4 trained, 0 controls. Subgoals and contradiction: inconclusive; author calls the subgoals teaching 'at best naive'.
quote: the fact that a student knows how to use a strategy is no guarantee whatsoever that the student will indeed use it
limits: N=7; no effect size, only a rank probability. Five practice sessions. Students often did not use a strategy they knew (one ignored fewer-variables on posttest Problem 1 until the 5-minute prompt). Controls were told every 5 minutes to stop and look over their work; the heuristics group was also told to look over the list, so a monitoring prompt is mixed in.
agent_relevance: Heuristic teaching worked for cue-driven, easily taught strategies and failed for vague ones. Knowing a heuristic is not using it, which is the control-layer problem in a 1979 lab study.

source: Hembree (1992) Experiments and relational studies in problem solving: a meta-analysis, JRME 23(3) (abstract via OpenAlex)
finding: 487 reports integrated. Training in diagrams and similar representations gave the largest gain. Heuristics: no method superior in grades K-5, mildly better in grades 6-8, distinctly superior in high school; teachers trained in heuristics also helped. Gap 5 (Hembree part): only the abstract was read; effect sizes not found.
numbers: 487 reports; no effect sizes in the abstract. Direction by grade: K-5 none, 6-8 mild, high school distinct.
quote: Heuristics in middle grades 6-8 seemed mildly better than other approaches and gained a distinctly superior status in high school.
limits: Only the abstract was opened. Numeric effect sizes by method remain unverified. Goldin (1992) criticised the meta-analysis (heterogeneous measures, no theory) and Hembree replied in JRME 23(3) 284-289 (not opened).
agent_relevance: Heuristic value grows with solver maturity and problem difficulty, which parallels strong models getting more from structure on hard tasks and little on easy ones.

source: Rott (2015) Rethinking heuristics: characterizations and vignettes, LUMAT 3(1)
finding: Applied three published coding manuals to the same three problem-solving vignettes. The number of actions counted as heuristic differs greatly by manual. Gap 10.
numbers: Same 32 actions: Koichu et al. manual codes 29 of 32 as heuristic, Kantowski 23 of 32, Rott 16 of 32. By vignette: 13/13, 10/13, 9/13; 11/13, 9/13, 7/13; 5/6, 4/6, 0/6. Rott's manual reached 85%+ interrater agreement; one 32-process check gave 84%. Earlier studies summarised: Kantowski 8 ninth graders, 5-month training; Koichu et al. 37 eighth graders, 5-month training; Rott 2012 32 fifth graders, significant moderate correlation of heuristic count with success.
limits: Three vignettes only; no test of the manual difference. Differences come mainly from metacognitive actions and algorithmic procedures.
agent_relevance: Measure heuristic use in agent traces with a fixed written coding rule and report interrater agreement; code metacognitive moves as a separate category so they are not counted as heuristics.

source: Huan, Li, Zheng and others (2025) Does math reasoning improve general LLM capabilities? Understanding transferability of LLM reasoning (ICLR 2026)
finding: Over 20 open reasoning-tuned models: most that succeed on math fail to carry gains to other reasoning, agent-planning, coding or instruction tasks. Controlled Qwen3-14B runs: RL on math transfers, SFT on math forgets. Gap 3 (training-time transfer only).
numbers: More than 20 models; controlled Qwen3-14B math-only data with RL versus SFT; the RL model generalised across domains, the SFT model drifted in latent space and token distribution. Per-domain deltas are in a bar figure, not extractable in text.
limits: Training-based transfer, not prompt-level heuristics, so it does not answer whether a Polya prompt transfers. Parameter updates differ from scaffolds.
agent_relevance: No LLM study of prompt-level heuristic transfer across problem families was found (gap 3 stays open). Plan tests with a held-out family per heuristic.

source: Breaking Barriers: Do reinforcement post-training gains transfer to unseen domains? (arXiv 2506.19733 v3), search snippet only
finding: Snippet only: RL post-training gains generalise within and across structured domains (math, code) but not to unstructured domains, across GRPO and DAPO. Not opened.
limits: Not opened; do not quote numbers. Training-time, not prompt-time.
agent_relevance: Same lesson as d16: transfer is limited by domain structure.
